quote: New genetic technologies are often expensive, and if genome editing becomes available only through private clinics, the benefits may flow mainly to wealthy families. This could deepen existing health inequalities, both within Australia and between wealthy and poorer countries. Rural and remote communities, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, and people on low incomes already face barriers to high-quality health care. There is also concern about genetic discrimination: if people are expected to edit their children’s genomes to avoid disease, those who cannot afford it, or who choose not to, may be blamed or penalised. Some fear the emergence of a genetic underclass.
